newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bombs kill three, wound 16 in Algeria - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bombs kill three, wound 16 in Algeria - paper.

text.p: Two bombs exploded in two Algerian towns over the weekend killing three people and wounding at least 16, an Algerian newspaper reported on Monday.
A car bomb targeted a security forces station in the coastal town of Gouraya, 90 km (55 miles) west of Algiers on Sunday. Two people were killed and several wounded, said El Watan.
The blast damaged houses, a local bank, a pharmacy and pylons and shattered windows of a school, it added.
The second bomb exploded at Zeboudja industrial centre in the western town of Chlef, 160 km (100 miles) from Algiers, killing at least one person and wounding 16, El Watan said.
No one claimed responsibility for the two attacks. The authorities have blamed Moslem guerrillas for a series of similar attacks in the past four years.

A report last month by a government-appointed human rights watchdog, the National Observatory of Human Rights (ONDH), said about 1,400 people had been killed in bombs attacks blamed on Moslem guerrillas in the past two years.

President Liamine Zeroual said on Saturday the security situation has improved this year compared to the last three years but acknowledged that rebel attacks would not be ended in "one or two months", although 2,000 fundamentalists had given in their weapons and repented.
An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
